children: Uniswap (UNI) fell on Saturday even as on-chain data showed selling pressure for UNI on Binance easing from its yearly high. The dip came two days before the token's futures debut on the CME Group (CME).

On Saturday, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost said in an X post that UNI is in a distribution phase. That is a point at which holders move tokens to exchanges to sell. He said it was driven by rising exchange inflows.

The analyst pointed out that UNI inflows to Binance were the highest of the year in late September, topping $40 million a day. During that period, the Z-score rose above four several times. The Z-score shows how many standard deviations a data point is from the mean, and a value above four is considered an extreme outlier.
Inflows have stayed fairly active since then, but Darkfost noted that the momentum “seems to be fading.”

He said UNI could find a bottom if that slowdown persists. That would end the distribution phase that started when the token peaked at $10.9. Since then, UNI has fallen over 30% from that level, he said.
traded at about $7.33, down 1.4% over 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around UNI remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.
Darkfost said the sell-off came after a strong run in Uniswap's fundamentals. He said total value locked (TVL), the value of assets deposited on the platform, exceeded $4 billion in September.
The decentralized exchange (DEX) volume reached an all-time high of $93.6 billion, according to the analyst. The token rallied as much as 370% from its June low, the analyst said.
DefiLlama data shows Uniswap's TVL at around $3.91 billion on Oct. 16. That was down from roughly $4.03 billion on Oct. 2.

title: Uniswap Slides Ahead Of CME Futures Debut As Binance Selling Pressure Eases
